title: Gas Station
statement: Stations are on a circular route. gas[i] fuel is available at station i and travelling to the next station costs cost[i]. Starting with an empty tank, return the index of the station from which you can complete the full circle clockwise, or -1 if impossible. If a solution exists it is unique.

hints.1_question: If the total gas is less than the total cost, no start works. Otherwise a start exists - how could a failure partway tell you where NOT to start?
hints.2_nudge: Run around once keeping the tank. If it goes negative at i, none of the stations from the current start through i can be the answer, so restart from i + 1.
hints.3_big_hint: If sum(gas) < sum(cost) return -1. Else start = tank = 0; for i: tank += gas[i]-cost[i]; if tank < 0: start = i+1; tank = 0. Return start.

known_bugs.name: starts at the first station where gas >= cost
known_bugs.followup: A station with enough gas for the first leg is not necessarily able to finish the whole circle. What about the later stretches?

known_bugs.name: never checks that a solution exists
known_bugs.followup: If the total gas is less than the total cost, can any starting station work? What does your code return then?

known_bugs.name: never moves the start after a failure
known_bugs.followup: When the tank goes negative at station i, which stations are now ruled out as starting points?

followups: Why is the start right after the last failure guaranteed to work when total gas >= total cost?
What if there could be several valid starts?
